title: Agent runtime starts each agent tab as a chat agent
story: Before this story every agent tab ran Claude Code in a terminal and the app typed into it. Now each tab starts a chat agent by default, the tab's waiting dot follows the agent's waiting events, and the live transcript, own-time 'use it' and Done reach the agent as one chat message. Until the chat view lands, the tab's terminal area shows the raw event stream; setting GRILLO_AGENT_RUNTIME=terminal brings the old terminal back.

checks.criterion: Starting an agent of any kind opens a tab whose agent is a chat agent; exactly one Claude Code process runs per tab
checks.steps: Start Grillo with GRILLO_AGENT_RUNTIME unset. Open a made-up project. Start a generic agent named 'qa-test'. Look at the tab and at the running processes.
checks.expected: One new tab named after the agent; its area shows the agent's event lines (init, assistant); exactly one claude process runs for that tab and no terminal shell is spawned beside it.

checks.criterion: The tab's waiting dot follows the chat protocol's waiting events
checks.steps: In the 'qa-test' tab, let the agent finish its first reply.
checks.expected: The waiting dot turns on when the agent's turn ends and turns off again when it starts working on the next message.

checks.criterion: The terminal stays as a fallback behind one runtime choice
checks.steps: Quit Grillo. Start it with GRILLO_AGENT_RUNTIME=terminal. Start a generic agent.
checks.expected: The tab shows an interactive terminal running Claude Code, as before this story.
